events.comment:
==== TEAM SELECTION MENU ====
Left card: your team. Right card: the roster, click a flag (or use the Left / Right keys) to pick your country. PLAY spins a red roulette over the other flags, lands on your opponent, then shows YOUR TEAM VS OPPONENT before the match starts.
The options window, saved settings, wide-screen interface and stadium ambience come from the OptionsMenu external events, linked below.
events.comment2: FSM Menu.State (Choosing, Drawing), written only in 'Menu transitions'. Choice stored in global Selection (PlayerCountry, OpponentCountry), read by Game. Country data: globals CountryList (tile order) and Countries[code].Name.

events.comment: At start, the mouse cursor is shown again (the match hides it) and each roster tile gets one country of the CountryList global variable, in reading order (left to right, top to bottom), with its name from Countries.
events.comment2: ForEach ordered by Y*10000+X asc; TileIndex = index in global CountryList, stored in the tile (Index()). Runs before the OptionsMenu link: SetCountry and SetClickable touch different tile children, order free.

events.comment: While the options window is open, the PLAY button and the flag tiles are switched off, so a click on the window never reaches them. They are switched back on when it closes.
events.comment2: If/Else pair: keep the Else right after its If. Trigger once in each branch: Activate/SetClickable written only on change (the Else also runs on frame 1). After the OptionsMenu link, so buttons go off the frame the window opens.

events.comment: The menu has two steps: Choosing (you pick your team) and Drawing (the opponent draw). PLAY starts the draw; once it is over, the match scene starts.
events.comment2: Only writer of Menu.State. Drawing entry resets MenuTimer (roulette, VS reveal, scene change) and requests the pointer lock during the real PLAY click (browsers need a user gesture).

events.comment: Your team card (left) always shows the selected country, and the choice is kept for the match.
events.comment2: Both states. Runs before the key and click handling below, so the card follows a change one frame later. Selection.PlayerCountry is read by the Game scene.

events.comment: Choosing: a click on a tile or the Left / Right keys change your team; your tile gets the yellow frame.
events.comment2: Highlight rewritten every frame from Menu.CountryIndex.

events.comment: Drawing: the opponent is drawn at once, then a red roulette jumps over the other flags and lands on it. Then the roster gives way to YOUR TEAM VS OPPONENT.
events.comment2: OpponentIndex never equals CountryIndex. RouletteTimer paces the jumps; MenuTimer (reset on entry) drives roulette end and VS reveal. Highlight loop repeated from Choosing on purpose: one block per state.

events.comment: Wide screens: keep the 2D menu centred on its 1920x1080 design.
events.comment2: UI layers (HUD, Modal) are centred in the OptionsMenu 'Screen layout' group; this scene also centres its base and Background layers.

events.comment:
==== INITIALIZATION ====
At the start of the scene, in this order: picks the two teams, sets up the camera, scoreboard and layers, dresses the flags and plays the player's anthem.
events.comment2: One action-less SceneJustBegins parent, sub-events run top to bottom. Teams first: everything after reads Match.PlayerCountry/OpponentCountry. Runs before the links, so every system sees the teams on frame 1.

events.comment: Teams: the player's country and the opponent come from the global Selection (team menu). Launched without the menu, the player is Selection.PlayerCountry (USA by default) and the opponent is drawn at random among the other countries.
events.comment2: First step: SetTeams, mallet clips, flags and anthem below read these countries. Empty opponent = player's country, so the While draws another one from CountryList. Adding a country: Countries + CountryList + CountryNames, GLB clips, flag animations, one anthem event.

events.comment: Screen: the 3D camera takes the position, height and tilt of the hidden Camera object and the field of view of CameraSettings, the step timer starts, the scoreboard receives the two teams, the Collisions and HUD layers (hidden in the editor) are shown and the mouse cursor is hidden.
events.comment2: Only the X tilt is copied here; the Intro state (MatchFlow) drives the camera from this same frame. StateTimer = Intro timer. SetTeams: opponent on the left, player on the right.

events.comment: Every flag around the table is the same object: its country comes from its side. Flags in the AI half show Match.OpponentCountry, the others Match.PlayerCountry.
events.comment2: Flag GLB clips are named after countries (USA, Belgium). Adding a country = one clip + one scoreboard flag animation, no new object.

events.comment: The player's anthem plays on channel 2 during the intro. Sound actions only take a fixed file name, so each country has its own event.
events.comment2: Anthem<Country>.mp3, volume 85. New country = one more event here.

events.comment:
==== GAME SYSTEMS ====
Each link below runs one external events sheet every frame, from top to bottom: options window, match steps, camera, player mallet, AI opponent, power-ups, puck and sounds, commentator, scoreboard, crowd, puck trail.
events.comment2: Link order = execution order, do not reorder: MatchFlow before CameraRig (intro camera), PuckAndSounds before Commentator (Commentator.NewHit*). Events below the links run last and override them.

events.comment:
==== OPTIONS BUTTON AND CURSOR ====
At the end of the match the OPTIONS button disappears, so it never covers the result window.
events.comment2: Runs after the OptionsMenu link, so it wins over its Activate(yes) on window close.

events.comment: In a match the mouse cursor is hidden; it shows while the options window is open, so its buttons can be clicked, and hides again when the window closes.
events.comment2: Trigger once per change. ShowCursor's Once must stay a sub-event: merged into the IsOpen event, the else-if below would fire while the window stays open. Not during Finished: MatchFlow shows the cursor for the result menu.

events.comment:
==== MATCH FLOW ====
The match goes through these steps, stored in the scene variable Match.State:
Intro -> Kickoff (puck placed in the centre, short pause) -> Playing -> Goal (celebration) -> Kickoff ...
The first team to score Match.GoalsToWin goals (5) wins: Finished (result menu).
Groups: Match transitions (when the step changes), Match states (what each step does), Match music.
events.comment2: FSM: Match.State written ONLY in 'Match transitions'; 'Match states' holds per-state actions (entry actions under Trigger once). StateTimer reset on every transition and at scene start. 'Match music' runs last.

events.comment: Decides WHEN the match changes step. Goals are detected here: the puck went past a goal line.
events.comment2: Puck origin is its centre (Model3D ModelOrigin). GoalLineMargin keeps a puck bouncing on the goal mouth from counting.

events.comment: After the goal celebration: the first team to reach Match.GoalsToWin goals wins the match, otherwise a new kickoff.
events.comment2: First to N goals: no clock, no draw. Single writer of Finished.

events.comment: What happens during each step. 'Trigger once' runs the first frame of a step only (placing the puck, showing a message...). Messages and the result menu are custom objects: we only call their actions.
events.comment2: SetX/SetY on Puck/mallet: one-off teleports at Kickoff entry (velocities zeroed right after) and the per-frame Goal clamp keeping the puck in the net. UI_* children are never touched here.

events.comment: Intro cinematic (match start): the camera circles around the field while the crowd does a wave, the two teams slide in from the sides to form the scoreboard in the middle of the screen, then the scoreboard goes up and the camera lands on the game position.
events.comment2: Progress = StateTimer / Match.IntroSeconds, smoothstep eased. The orbit ends on the Camera object (angle, distance from field centre); the last 20% (CameraLanding) lerps tilt, Y rotation and angle to it, Kickoff entry then copies it exactly. Knobs: CameraSettings.Intro*, ScoreboardCentreY/TopY.

parameters: ToDeg(atan2(Camera.X() - Field.CenterX, Camera.Y() - Field.CenterY)) + CameraSettings.IntroStartAngle * (1 - Eased)
lerp(CameraSettings.IntroRadius, DistanceBetweenPositions(Field.CenterX, Field.CenterY, Camera.X(), Camera.Y()), Eased)

events.comment: A puck that entered a goal never comes back out: during Goal it is braked every frame and kept behind the goal line of the scored goal.
events.comment2: LastScorer Player = top goal (Y < Field.Top), Opponent = bottom goal (Y > Field.Bottom). Clamp against the goal line + puck radius; back walls stop it at the net.

events.comment: Victory confetti: when a team wins (not on a draw), bursts of confetti pop all around the field.
events.comment2: Confetti = asset store 3D particle emitter (ParticleEmitter3D), it deletes itself once the confetti fell.

events.comment: The match music starts once the anthem of the intro has finished (sound channel 2).
events.comment2: Match.MusicStarted keeps it from restarting; MatchMusic loops. Not a Match.State step: own group, still the last event of the sheet.

events.comment:
==== PLAYER MALLET ====
The player's mallet follows the mouse (or the finger) but stays inside the player's half of the field. The Physics3D behavior moves it: the events only give it a speed toward a target point.
- Pointer lock: turns the mouse or the finger into a virtual cursor.
- Mallet movement: places that cursor on the player's half and moves the mallet toward it.
events.comment2: Kinematic body driven only via SetLinearVelocityX/Y (single position owner = Physics3D). 'Pointer lock' writes PointerLock.U/V before 'Mallet movement' reads them, same frame.

events.comment: Pointer lock: the PLAY click (Menu) and the replay click already lock the mouse, so the match starts locked; otherwise a click during the match locks it (no cursor leaving the window). The options window and the result menu release it. Locked, the mouse movement moves a virtual cursor (PointerLock.U/V, from 0 to 1 over the screen); unlocked or on touch, U/V follow the real cursor.
events.comment2: Extension MousePointerLock (store). Lock request first, then the locked / unlocked branches (if / else). PointerLock.Speed scales the locked movement; browsers only grant the lock during a real click.

events.comment:
The virtual cursor (PointerLock.U/V, from 0 to 1 over the whole screen) is placed on the player's half of the field: that is the target point.
Sensitivity (OPTIONS window, 1 to 10) is the share of the distance to the target covered each frame: at 10 the mallet sticks to the cursor, lower values make it follow more smoothly.
Once the match is finished, the mallet stops.
events.comment2: FollowShare = 1 - (1 - S/10)^(TimeDelta*60): frame-rate independent, 0 when paused (TimeDelta 0). Velocity = gap * FollowShare / TimeDelta, capped at Tuning.Player.MaxSpeed. S = global Settings.MalletSensitivity.

events.comment:
==== OPPONENT AI ====
The computer mallet (its country is drawn at random before the match) is driven by a state machine: its object variable State says what it is doing.
- Idle: the match is not being played, go back in front of the goal.
- Defend: stay on the guard line in front of the goal and follow the puck sideways.
- Attack: rush the puck when it is in the AI half, in front of the mallet.
- Strike: during some attacks, a sharp hit through the puck.
- Unstick: move forward for a moment when the mallet is stuck.
events.comment2: FSM: State written ONLY in 'Opponent transitions'. Run order: transitions, aim mistakes, states (target per state), one movement event. Physics3D kinematic velocity like PlayerMallet. Difficulty knobs: Tuning.Opponent.*.

events.comment:
Decides WHEN the AI changes state. Only this group writes State.
Match not being played -> Idle. Otherwise: Idle -> Defend at once; Defend -> Attack when the puck enters the AI half in front of the mallet; Attack -> Defend when the puck leaves, or -> Strike when close enough; Strike -> Defend after a short hit; any state -> Unstick when the mallet is stuck; Unstick -> Defend after a moment.
events.comment2: Runs before the other groups: a transition takes effect the same frame. Siblings run in order and re-test State, so one frame can chain transitions (Idle -> Defend -> Attack).

events.comment: Leaving Attack: back to Defend when the puck left the AI half or slipped behind the mallet. Otherwise, if a strike was planned when the attack started and the AI no longer hesitates, it strikes as soon as the puck is close enough.
events.comment2: No Or here: an Or whose branches do not all mention MalletOpponent picks no mallet when only the puck branch is true, so State was never written. Else-if chain: Strike only when no retreat happened this frame. StrikePlanned / ReactionDelay set on Attack entry.

events.comment: Anti-stuck: if the mallet barely moved for Tuning.Opponent.StuckSeconds (and is not frozen by a power-up), it moves forward for a moment (state Unstick), then defends again.
events.comment2: Movement measured from an anchor (AnchorX/Y) reset each time the mallet leaves a Tuning.Opponent.StuckDistance radius. StillSeconds is also reset when the match is not playing and on Unstick entry.

events.comment: Human-like mistakes: every Tuning.Opponent.AimRefreshSeconds the AI picks a new aiming error and a new speed, and takes a snapshot of where the puck is. Defend follows that snapshot, not the live puck: the AI reacts late, so fast shots can score.
events.comment2: Runs every frame in every state, between the transitions and the states. AimErrorX in +/-Tuning.Opponent.AimError px, SpeedFactor in [Tuning.Opponent.SpeedFactorMin, 1], TrackedPuckX = puck X snapshot.

events.comment:
What each state does: it chooses a target point, a follow gain and a max speed.
- Idle: in front of the goal.
- Defend: on the guard line, following the puck snapshot sideways.
- Attack: the live puck (after a possible hesitation).
- Strike: a point past the puck, very fast, to hit through it.
- Unstick: straight forward.
The last event moves the mallet toward that target.
events.comment2: Locals TargetX/TargetY/FollowGain are declared on the next event: each state sub-event fills them, the last sub-event reads them. Speed cap per state in the object variable CurrentMaxSpeed.

events.comment: Human reactions: when an attack starts, the AI sometimes hesitates a random moment before moving (it stays where it is), each attack gets its own random speed, and the AI decides whether this attack will end with a strike.
events.comment2: Trigger once = first frame of the Attack state. Tuning.Opponent.HesitationChance (0..1), HesitationMaxSeconds, SpeedFactorMin, StrikeChance. StrikePlanned and ReactionDelay are read by the Attack -> Strike transition.

events.comment: Movement, whatever the state: the target is kept inside the AI half of the field, then the mallet gets a speed proportional to its distance to the target (follow gain), capped at the max speed of the state.
events.comment2: Same kinematic velocity pattern as PlayerMallet (Physics3D is the only position owner). If State matches no state event, the local defaults (960, 130, gain 6) and the last CurrentMaxSpeed apply.

events.comment:
==== PUCK AND IMPACT SOUNDS ====
Everything that happens to the puck, one group per job: it stays flat and under a speed limit, it is put back on the field if it slips out, it makes a sound on impacts, the mallets hit it, and it is nudged when it gets stuck.
events.comment2: Reads PowerUps.PuckSpeedCap (set by PowerUps). Writes Match.LastHitter and Commentator.NewHitBy/NewHitSpeed on each new touch. Mallet/puck contact is solved by events (group Mallet hit), not by Physics3D.

events.comment:
==== PUCK FLAT AND SPEED CAP ====
The Physics3D behavior makes the puck slide and bounce. Here the puck is kept flat on the table (except during a goal) and its speed is limited so that players can follow it.
events.comment2: Velocity Z and Z forced to 0 each frame except in Goal state. Cap = PowerUps.PuckSpeedCap (Tuning.Puck.MaxSpeed, or PowerUps.TurboMaxSpeed during Turbo): X/Y rescaled, direction kept.

events.comment:
==== SAFETY NET ====
If the puck ever squeezes through a border (pushed by a mallet against the rim), it is put back on the field and sent back toward the centre. In front of each goal the puck may cross the end line: that is how it scores.
events.comment2: One-off teleport under a guard (allowed by rule 1). No Y clamp in the goal gap |X - Field.CenterX| <= Field.GoalHalfWidth. Velocity sign forced back toward the field.

events.comment:
==== IMPACT SOUNDS ====
A short sound plays when the puck starts touching a mallet or a wall.
events.comment2: Physics3D CollisionStarted, one event per object (different picking, so not factored). PuckHit pitch 1 for the player mallet, 0.9 for the opponent.

events.comment:
==== MALLET HIT ====
Rocket League style hit (copied from soccar): the mallets do NOT collide physically with the puck, the hit is computed here for each mallet touching it. The puck is put back at the mallet edge, takes the mallet speed along the contact line with a little friction, gets an extra kick on the first frame of the touch, and always leaves at a minimum speed. Walls, corners and goal backs stay handled by the physics engine (Jolt, default settings).
events.comment2: Mallets have Physics3D layers/masks 4: no contact with the puck. Touch = Distance < Mallets.Radius + Field.PuckRadius, not in Goal state. Mallets var IsTouchingPuck marks a running touch. Steps below run in this order, each reads the puck velocity left by the previous one.

parameters: clamp(Mallets.X() + NormalX * (Mallets.Radius + Field.PuckRadius), Field.Left + Field.PuckRadius, Field.Right - Field.PuckRadius)
clamp(Mallets.Y() + NormalY * (Mallets.Radius + Field.PuckRadius), Field.Top + Field.PuckRadius, Field.Bottom - Field.PuckRadius)

events.comment: Puck pinned against a wall: the mallet pushes it into a border, so it could not be put back at the mallet edge. It is pushed along the wall instead (toward the centre in a corner), so it always gets free.
events.comment2: Pinned = still overlapping by more than 1 px after the clamp. Normal component into a side/end wall zeroed, fallback sign(Field.CenterX - X) if both zero, then renormalised and ClosingSpeed recomputed.

events.comment: The mallet moves toward the puck: the puck takes the mallet speed along the contact line (no bounce), and a little friction drags it sideways with the mallet.
events.comment2: ClosingSpeed > 0 only. v += (1 + Tuning.Hit.Restitution) * ClosingSpeed * n - FrictionSpeed * tangent; tangent slip cut by min(slip * Tuning.Hit.FrictionShare, 2 * ClosingSpeed).

events.comment: First frame of a touch: an extra kick along the mallet-to-puck line, proportionally stronger on slow touches. The mallet becomes the last hitter (used by the power-ups and the commentator).
events.comment2: IsTouchingPuck false = touch start. ExtraSpeed = min(relative speed, Tuning.Hit.ExtraSpeedCap) * scale; scale goes ExtraLowScale -> ExtraMidScale -> ExtraHighScale between ExtraLowSpeed, ExtraMidSpeed and ExtraSpeedCap.

parameters: Tuning.Hit.ExtraLowScale + (Tuning.Hit.ExtraMidScale - Tuning.Hit.ExtraLowScale) * clamp((ExtraSpeed - Tuning.Hit.ExtraLowSpeed) / (Tuning.Hit.ExtraMidSpeed - Tuning.Hit.ExtraLowSpeed), 0, 1) + (Tuning.Hit.ExtraHighScale - Tuning.Hit.ExtraMidScale) * clamp((ExtraSpeed - Tuning.Hit.ExtraMidSpeed) / (Tuning.Hit.ExtraSpeedCap - Tuning.Hit.ExtraMidSpeed), 0, 1)

events.comment: Whatever happened above, the puck always leaves the mallet at a minimum speed, so it never stays glued to it (even against a wall). Then the mallet remembers that it touches the puck.
events.comment2: Relative normal speed, read again after the impulses above, raised to Tuning.Hit.MinSeparationSpeed. Must stay after them. IsTouchingPuck set True here, set False by the next event once the mallet is away.

events.comment:
==== STUCK PUCK ====
A puck that stays almost still for a while (typically wedged in a corner behind the AI guard line, where no mallet goes) is nudged toward the centre of the field.
events.comment2: Playing state only. Speed < Tuning.Puck.StuckSpeed for Tuning.Puck.StuckSeconds -> velocity Tuning.Puck.NudgeSpeed toward (Field.CenterX, Field.CenterY). Puck var StillSeconds, reset by the Else.

events.comment:
==== SCOREBOARD ====
Sends the score (opponent on the left, player on the right), the goal to reach and the time played to the scoreboard object. The formatting lives inside UI_Scoreboard.
events.comment2: Only calls UI_Scoreboard actions (SetScore, SetClock); never touches its children. Clock = Match.ElapsedSeconds (counts up, first to GoalsToWin).

events.comment:
==== STADIUM CROWD ====
The spectators cheer all the time (clip Cheer). They start a Mexican wave (clip Wave) that runs once around the stands: at random every few seconds, on every goal, and during the match intro.
events.comment2: FSM on Stadium.State (Cheer, Wave), written only in 'Crowd transitions', applied in 'Crowd states'. Tuning: Crowd.WaveCheckSeconds, WaveChanceOneIn, IntroWaveDelaySeconds. Wave = 16 shape keys (one per stand sector) in Stadium.glb.

events.comment: Normal life of the crowd: while it cheers, a countdown runs. Each time it reaches zero, there is one chance in Crowd.WaveChanceOneIn that a Mexican wave starts. Once the wave animation has played, the crowd cheers again.
events.comment2: Countdown = object variable Stadium.WaveCheckCooldown, refilled with Crowd.WaveCheckSeconds. Wave end = HasAnimationEnded (the Wave clip is not looped).

events.comment: Every goal starts a Mexican wave (if one is not already running).
events.comment2: Trigger once on Match.State = Goal; the random draw above still adds waves between goals.

events.comment: The intro cinematic of a match starts with the crowd cheering, then a Mexican wave after a short delay.
events.comment2: Intro entry: Cheer + object timer IntroWave; wave once the timer passes Crowd.IntroWaveDelaySeconds.

events.comment: What each state does: on the frame the state starts, the stadium plays the matching animation (Cheer loops, Wave plays once).
events.comment2: Trigger once per state: the clip is set only on entry. Runs after 'Crowd transitions', so a new state's clip starts the same frame.

events.comment:
==== PUCK TRAIL ====
A flat white ribbon follows the puck on the field: every frame a short segment is laid between the previous and the current puck position, then it thins out and disappears.
events.comment2: PuckTrail = flat Cube3D (top face only, soft band texture, Basic material, no shadow). Tuning in TrailSettings (Width px, LifeSeconds, MinStep px). A jump bigger than 200 px (kickoff teleport) draws nothing.

events.comment: Every frame during play, a segment is laid between the previous and the current puck position. Tiny moves (under TrailSettings.MinStep) and jumps of 200 px or more (the puck put back at kickoff) draw nothing.
events.comment2: StepLength = local variable. Segment: centre = midpoint, width = StepLength + 6 px overlap, height = TrailSettings.Width, angle of the step, Z 3 above the table, Life 1.

events.comment: Remember the puck position for the next frame. A sub-event, so it runs AFTER the segment is laid (parent actions run before sub-events).
events.comment2: Must stay the LAST sub-event: the segment above reads Puck.TrailLastX/Y as last frame's position. Runs in every match state.

events.comment: Each segment gets thinner as its Life goes from 1 to 0 in TrailSettings.LifeSeconds, then it is deleted.
events.comment2: SetCenter after SetHeight: resizing keeps the top-left corner, so the stored CenterX/Y is applied again to keep the segment on the puck path.

events.comment:
==== CAMERA RIG ====
Outside the intro, the game camera sits on the Camera object, plus a very light parallax that follows the mouse, plus a short shake after each goal.
events.comment2: Runs after MatchFlow (the intro drives the camera itself). Parallax: mouse position on the HUD layer (screen pixels) mapped to -1..1, smoothed by CameraSettings.ParallaxFollowSpeed. Shake: CameraRig.ShakeTimeLeft set on Goal entry, random offset fading linearly.

parameters: lerp(CameraRig.ParallaxOffsetX, clamp((MouseX("HUD", 0) - SceneWindowWidth() / 2) / (SceneWindowWidth() / 2), -1, 1) * CameraSettings.ParallaxX, min(1, CameraSettings.ParallaxFollowSpeed * TimeDelta()))

lerp(CameraRig.ParallaxOffsetY, clamp((MouseY("HUD", 0) - SceneWindowHeight() / 2) / (SceneWindowHeight() / 2), -1, 1) * CameraSettings.ParallaxY, min(1, CameraSettings.ParallaxFollowSpeed * TimeDelta()))

events.comment: Each goal shakes the camera: the shake starts on the first frame of the goal and fades out in the event above.
events.comment2: Trigger once on Goal entry, placed after the follow event: the offset shows from the next frame, fading over CameraSettings.ShakeSeconds (amplitude CameraSettings.ShakeAmplitude).

events.comment:
==== OPTIONS WINDOW ====
Shared by the Menu and Game scenes (linked in both). The gear button (or the Escape key) opens the options window: sound volume and mallet speed. Settings are saved on the device and loaded once when the game starts. This sheet also keeps the interface centred on wide screens and plays the stadium ambience.
events.comment2: Settings = global structure, persisted in storage AirHockey (Volume, MalletSensitivity). UI_OptionsModal and OptionsButton are global objects (both scenes); the modal is a self-hiding custom object on the Modal layer, so no external layout (OVERLAY_IN_SCENE ignored).

events.comment: Once per game launch, read the saved settings (if any). At the start of every scene, the saved sound volume is applied.
events.comment2: Settings.IsLoaded guards the load; globals survive scene changes, so it runs once. Missing storage elements keep the defaults. The load runs before SetGlobalVolume, in the same first frame.

events.comment: The gear button opens the window with the current settings. While it is open, every change is applied right away (volume) and saved on the device.
events.comment2: Volume() / Sensitivity() are read from the modal; compared to Settings so storage is written only on change.

events.comment: Escape key: closes the options window if it is open, otherwise opens it (for keyboard players; the gear button is for touch and mouse).
events.comment2: Open only while OptionsButton is activated: it is off while the window is open and at the end of a match (Game sheet).

events.name: Pause while the options window is open

events.comment: While the options window is open, the Modal layer is shown, the game is paused and the gear button is switched off. When it closes, the layer is hidden, the game resumes and the gear button works again.
events.comment2: Modal layer hidden in the editor and at launch (both scenes). Time scale 0 freezes timers, physics and TimeDelta movement. If/Else pair, Trigger once in each branch: written only on change (the Else also runs on frame 1).

events.comment: Wide screens: the game widens its resolution (adaptWidth) instead of black bars. UI layers keep their camera on the 1920x1080 design centre, so the interface stays centred.
events.comment2: Modal scrims extend far past 1920x1080 in their variants to cover any width. Layers missing in a scene are ignored.

events.comment: Background crowd ambience in every scene (menu and match): a random track among Ambient1..N plays quietly on its own channel, the next one starts when it ends. Sound effects and voices play over it.
events.comment2: Global Ambience.Channel (5), Volume, TrackCount (3). New track = AmbientN.mp3 resource + TrackCount + one Track = N event (sound actions take a fixed file name).

events.comment:
==== POWER-UPS ====
During play, a power-up token appears on the field every few seconds. When the puck rolls over it, the power goes to the mallet that touched the puck last: BIG MALLET (bigger mallet), FREEZE (the other mallet cannot move), TURBO PUCK (faster puck) or GOAL SHIELD (a wall protects your goal).
events.comment2: Tuning in scene structure PowerUps. Match.LastHitter = Mallets.ObjectName() written by PuckAndSounds on each new touch. Linked after OpponentAI so FREEZE overrides both mallet velocities; reads Match.State, never writes it.

events.comment:
==== RESET AT KICKOFF ====
Every kickoff starts clean: no token, no shield, no running power.
events.comment2: Trigger once per Kickoff entry. Also restarts the scene timer PowerUpSpawn and clears Match.LastHitter.

events.comment:
==== TOKENS ====
A token appears at a random spot when none is on the field, spins on itself, and vanishes if nobody takes it in time.
events.comment2: CreateByName picks the object PowerUp<Kind> of group PowerUpTokens; Cube3D position = top-left corner, size 110.

events.comment: A thin white circle is laid around the new token: it shows how long the token stays on the field.
events.comment2: RingSegments overlapping Cube3D pieces (10 x 6) on a circle of RingRadius, from 12 o'clock; Step = order of disappearance. Cube3D position = top-left.

events.comment: The white circle empties like a clock as the token gets old, and its opacity pulses (faster for the last moments). It disappears with its token.
events.comment2: Cube3D has no opacity action: the front face texture is swapped among PowerUpRing100/80/60/40/25 (white with that alpha) from a sine. Pieces with Step >= RingSegments x remaining share are deleted.

events.comment:
==== PICKUP ====
The puck rolls over a token: the power goes to the last mallet that hit the puck, and its name is announced for a short time.
events.comment2: Kind = object name without the PowerUp prefix. Only one token exists at a time, so expressions on PowerUpTokens read that one. Announcement hidden after PowerUps.MessageSeconds (scene timer PowerUpMessage).

events.comment: GOAL SHIELD: a white wall and a shield icon appear in front of the goal of the mallet that took the power. A shield it already had is replaced.
events.comment2: Owner = Match.LastHitter. The last event acts on every GoalShield/GoalShieldIcon (Create picking is not shared between siblings): safe while only one shield can exist (EffectSeconds < SpawnSeconds).

events.comment:
==== RUNNING POWERS ====
Powers run for a few seconds. A big mallet grows (and hits with a bigger radius), a frozen mallet cannot move, a turbo puck can go faster, a goal shield disappears when its time is up.
events.comment2: Actions on group Mallets run per instance with its own Effects. Inverse conditions instead of Else: Else fails with per-instance picking, and the <= 0 event must also run on the frame the countdown ends.

events.comment:
==== COMMENTATOR ====
Short voice reactions at precise moments: kickoff, saves, good hits, near misses, dead time, goals and the end of the match. One line at a time: 'Commentator triggers' chooses the line, 'Commentator voice' says it.
events.comment2: Queue: Commentator.PendingLine, dropped after PendingTimeLeft. Played by native PlaySoundOnChannel, one event per line (Language fr = voice/fr, else voice/default). Random picks from Commentator.Lines arrays.

events.comment: Decides WHICH line to say, and only queues it ('Commentator voice' says it). Big moments (first kickoff, near misses, goals, end of the match) replace the queued line; small reactions (hits, dead time, 'here we go again') wait until the queue is free.
events.comment2: NewHitBy / NewHitSpeed are written by PuckAndSounds on the first frame of each mallet touch, and cleared here.

events.comment: Timers: the pause between two hit reactions and the waiting time of the queued line count down, the time since the player's last touch counts up.
events.comment2: HitCooldown, PendingTimeLeft (the voice group drops the queued line at <= 0), SincePlayerTouch (reset by the player's touches).

events.comment: Kickoff: reset the rally counters. Before the first kickoff of the match the commentator says 'go go go'; after an opponent goal, 'here we go again'.
events.comment2: Trigger once on Match.State = Kickoff. 'Here we go again' only if no line is still queued (a goal line keeps priority). Both lines may wait 3 s for a free channel.

events.comment: Each new touch of the puck: count the player's touches in the rally, and sometimes react to the player's saves and good hits.
events.comment2: Save = player touch with the puck in the bottom SaveZoneHeight px ('08_nice'). Strong hit = NewHitSpeed >= StrongHitSpeed, chance HitChance; other hits HitChance / 2. A chosen line waits 1 s max, then HitCooldownSeconds of rest.

events.comment: The touch has been handled: clear it so it is counted only once.
events.comment2: Must stay the LAST sub-event: the touch cases above still read NewHitBy (parent actions run before sub-events).

events.comment: While the puck is in play: count the side-wall bounces, react to near misses and fill the dead time.
events.comment2: Action-less guard on Match.State = Playing (written by MatchFlow only). Order inside: bounces, near misses, dead time.

events.comment: Side-wall bounces since the last touch (the sideways speed changes sign), for the 'nothing but net' goal.
events.comment2: Compares with Commentator.LastVelocityX (last frame's X speed, stored after this block). A touch resets the count in the touch block above.

events.comment: Near misses: a fast shot hits the end wall right next to a goal post. The player's shot beside the opponent goal ('that's terrible') or the opponent's shot beside the player's goal ('nooo', 'yikes') queues a line and plays the crowd near-miss sound.
events.comment2: Post zone: GoalHalfWidth..GoalHalfWidth + NearMissPostWidth px from Field.CenterX, within 15 px of the end wall, speed > NearMissMinSpeed. Local NearMissLine = line chosen by the case. NearMissArmed: once per touch, re-armed by the next touch and at kickoff.

events.comment: Dead time: when the puck has barely moved for 2 seconds, the commentator urges the players on ('go go go').
events.comment2: Puck slower than IdleSpeed for IdleLineSeconds; IdleSeconds then goes negative (IdleRepeatSeconds) so it is not repeated at once.

events.comment: Remember the puck's sideways speed for the bounce test of the next frame. Done in every match state, so the first frame of play never compares with an old speed.
events.comment2: Must stay after the Playing block and outside it: the bounce test reads last frame's value, and a stale value from before a goal would count a fake bounce.

events.comment: Goals. Player goal: a direct shot (no side-wall bounce since the player's touch) is 'nothing but net', a long player rally is 'scored', otherwise a random goal cry. Opponent goal: an own goal (last touch by the player) gets an own-goal line, otherwise 'oh noo'.
events.comment2: Trigger once on Match.State = Goal. Replaces any queued line and stops the one being said on Commentator.Channel, so the goal line starts at once (may wait 5 s).

events.comment: End of the match: 'good game' on a win; on a defeat 'not bad' (3+ goals), 'what was the plan' (1-2 goals) or 'oh no' (no goal).
events.comment2: Trigger once on Match.State = Finished. Replaces any queued line and stops the one being said on Commentator.Channel; the final line may wait 8 s for a free channel.

events.comment: Says the queued line as soon as nobody else is talking, or drops it when it waited too long.
events.comment2: Free = channel 3 and Commentator.Channel (4) both silent. Nothing plays on channel 3 since the country commentary was removed: that test always passes (kept, harmless).

events.comment: Plays the queued line, then empties the queue. Sound actions only accept a fixed file name, so there is one event per line, on purpose: French recordings when Commentator.Language is "fr", English otherwise. Both lists are folded: unfold them to add a line.
events.comment2: voice/fr/ or voice/default/<line>.mp3; no native way to compute a resource name, and no JS. New line = one event in each branch. New language = one more branch. Browser language is not read.

eventsFunctionsExtensions.shortDescription: Lock and hide mouse pointer for unlimited movement (e.g., FPS mouse look).
description: This behavior removes the limit on the distance the mouse can move and hides the cursor.
For example, a user can rotate or continue to manipulate an object by moving the mouse endlessly ([open the project online](https://editor.gdevelop.io/?project=example://mouse-pointer-lock)).
Without the pointer lock, the rotation or operation will stop the moment the pointer reaches the edge of the browser or screen.
Game players don't have to worry about leaving the gameplay area or accidentally clicking on another application that moves the mouse focus away from the game.
Locking the pointer locks `CursorX()` and `CursorY()` expressions.
